title: Direct investment positions by counterpart economy (IMF DIP, formerly CDIS): Lebanon as reporter, and partner economies reporting positions with Lebanon (mirror), 2009-2024
source: IMF, Direct Investment Positions by Counterpart Economy (DIP), dataflow IMF.STA:DIP

redistribute_note: Mark as redistribute:false like the IMF WEO files until someone reads the IMF terms: show with attribution, keep out of CSV downloads and out of the CC BY-SA claim.
citation: International Monetary Fund. Direct Investment Positions by Counterpart Economy, https://data.imf.org/en/datasets/IMF.STA:DIP. Accessed 2026-10-05.
unit: US$ million at year end (the API returns US dollars with SCALE=6; converted here by dividing by 1,000,000; checked against USA outward position in Canada 2023 = 426,255 million)
notes: Positions (stocks) at year end, not annual flows. dv_type O = reported by the reporting economy; SCC = derived by IMF from the counterpart economy's report (mirror). Rows with reporter LBN: Lebanon's own reports (O) and what partners report about Lebanon (SCC). Rows with counterpart LBN: what each partner reports about Lebanon (O) and Lebanon's report about that partner (SCC). Net means liabilities less assets for inward and assets less liabilities for outward, as the IMF code list labels them; it can differ from gross figures in other FDI tables. Lebanon reports many zeros and gaps, so the partner-reported (mirror) side is the usable one for origin: compare dv_type O rows with reporter LBN against dv_type O rows with counterpart LBN. Only series with at least one non-zero value are listed; absent series are zero or unreported. Counterpart codes follow IMF: ISO3 for most economies, plus IMF aggregates such as G001 World, U150 Europe, GX451 Economies of Persian Gulf, GX454 Other Near and Middle East Economies, WBG West Bank and Gaza. Aggregates overlap with countries, so never sum a column. 2023 and 2024 cover far fewer series than 2011-2022.
